title: Quantitative analysis of cells encapsulated in a scaffold
author: Egorikhina, Aleynik, et al.

steps.title: Prepare and stain scaffold fragment
steps.instruction: Place a scaffold fragment of at least 0.64 cm² into a well of a 24‑well fluorescence microscopy plate with opaque side walls (e.g., Black Visiplate™ TC plate). Add 2 mL of the appropriate culture medium (e.g., DMEM or α‑MEM with 10 % fetal calf serum). Add 1 µL of Hoechst 33342 solution (10 µg · mL⁻¹, USA). Incubate 30 min at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Place fragment in well of 24‑well plate with opaque walls.
Add 2 mL culture medium (type matching the cells, e.g., DMEM or α‑MEM + 10 % FCS).
Add 1 µL Hoechst 33342 (10 µg · mL⁻¹).
Incubate 30 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash stained scaffold
steps.instruction: Remove the dye medium and wash the fragment twice with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS): add 2 mL PBS, incubate 10 min at room temperature, discard PBS; repeat once. Finally, add 0.3–1 mL PBS to keep the sample moist.

substeps.instruction: Discard the Hoechst‑containing medium.
Add 2 mL PBS, incubate 10 min at RT, discard.
Repeat the PBS wash once more.
Add 0.3–1 mL PBS to prevent drying.

steps.title: Acquire Z‑stack images
steps.instruction: Transfer the plate to a fluorescence microscope equipped with Z‑stack capability (e.g., Cytation 5 with Gen5 software). Use the Hoechst channel (excitation 377 nm, emission 477 nm) and a 4× or 10× objective. For each of at least five fields of view, capture a Z‑stack from the surface to a maximum depth of 530 µm, then stitch the stack into a single focused image.

substeps.instruction: Place plate on microscope with Z‑stack function.
Select Hoechst channel (377 nm ex / 477 nm em).
Choose 4× or 10× objective.
For each field (≥5), acquire images at successive Z positions up to 530 µm depth.
Stitch the Z‑stack into one fully focused image.

steps.title: Process images and count nuclei
steps.instruction: Open each stitched Z‑stack image in Gen5 Image software. Apply a fluorescence intensity threshold filter (include only objects with intensity > 7000) and an object‑area filter (include only objects with area < 30 µm²). Count the remaining objects as cell nuclei. Verify inclusion of all nuclei by applying the “mask” function and visually inspecting the result.

substeps.instruction: Load stitched image into Gen5.
Set intensity threshold > 7000.
Set area filter < 30 µm².
Count objects that meet both criteria.
Optionally apply mask and visually confirm that all nuclei are captured.

steps.title: Calculate cell density per mm³
steps.instruction: From at least ten stitched images, record the total number of nuclei per image, compute the average (N). Measure the field‑of‑view dimensions: B (X‑axis µm) and C (Y‑axis µm) for the chosen magnification, and D (Z‑axis µm) which is the Z‑stack depth (≤ 530 µm). Calculate cells per mm³ using K = N × B × C × D × 10⁻⁹.

substeps.instruction: Count nuclei in ≥10 stitched images.
Calculate average nuclei per image (N).
Record field‑of‑view size: B (µm, X), C (µm, Y), D (µm, Z).
Apply formula K = N * B * C * D * 10⁻⁹ to obtain cells per mm³.

steps.title: Assess proliferative activity over time
steps.instruction: Culture the cell‑laden scaffold under standard conditions (37 °C, humidified 5 % CO₂) for up to 14 days. At chosen time points (e.g., days 1, 3, 7, 10, 14), excise a fragment of at least 0.64 cm² and perform steps 1‑5 on each fragment. Compare the calculated cell densities across time points to evaluate proliferation.

substeps.instruction: Maintain scaffold in appropriate growth medium at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
At each scheduled day, cut a ≥0.64 cm² fragment.
Perform staining, washing, imaging, processing, and calculation as described in steps 1‑5.
Compile cell‑density values for each time point and analyze trends.
